exposure: Obese women (class I, II, and III)
BMI categories: underweight, normal weight, overweight, class I obesity, class II obesity, and class III obesity
Weight gain categories: insufficient (<11 lbs), adequate (11-20 lbs), and excessive (>20 lbs)
cohort: 60,431 women from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) in the US
finding: Class I and II obese women who gained excessive weight during pregnancy had increased odds of cesarean delivery compared to those with adequate weight gain, while weight gain did not significantly affect cesarean risk in class III obese women.
mod_finding: Excessive weight gain during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of cesarean delivery in class I and II obese women, but not in class III obese women.
